title: Dimsplice embeddings + rerank breadcrumbs (personal)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the weird rerank endpoint anomalies observed 2026-03-07 -> 2026-03-09. Primary symptoms: intermittent dimension mismatch errors returned to clients, and correlated 95th-percentile latency spikes for rerank requests. Notes are messy — chronological, commands I ran, raw snippets, and hypotheses for handoff to SRE/ML infra.

Summary of observed behavior:
- Rerank service (v2) returned DimensionMismatchError to several customers between 03-07 22:30 and 03-08 03:15 PST. Error message: "DimensionMismatchError: expected embedding dim 1536 but got 1024" (exact message captured in logs).
- Same time window: 95p latency for rerank route jumped from ~120ms -> ~900ms for ~12-20 minute windows, then dropped back. Not constant — appears bursty.
- Affected traffic sampled shows majority of requests routed to model variant "open-3b-quant" on Dedicated pool; fallback to hosted variants sometimes occurred.

What I reproduced locally (quick steps):
1) POST a rerank payload with embeddings produced by local encoder of different dim:
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/run/rerank \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"query_embedding": [0.1, 0.2, ... (1536 floats) ...], "candidate_embeddings": [[...1536 floats...],[...1536 floats...]], "top_k": 5}'

2) Simulate accidental 1024-dim input:
   - I truncated the vector and hit same endpoint. Observed immediate 400 with DimensionMismatchError in client response. Server logs included stack trace (copy below).

Server log excerpt (scrubbed timestamps and request ids):
----- BEGIN LOG -----
ERROR rerank.handler:400 DimensionMismatchError: expected 1536 got 1024
  File "/srv/serving/rerank.py", line 298, in handle_rerank
    assert emb.shape[-1] == model_config.emb_dim
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/numpy/core/fromnumeric.py", line 89, in reshape
    raise DimensionMismatchError
Caused-by: client-side truncated payload? upstream conversion?
----- END LOG -----

Latency trace snippet (stacked traces correlated with request id):
- 2026-03-08T00:42:12Z request_id=abc123 route=/rerank model=open-3b-quant
  runtime: request-queue 350ms, model-init 0ms, tokenize 12ms, inference 320ms, postproc 14ms -> total 696ms
- 2026-03-08T00:42:45Z request_id=def456 route=/rerank model=open-3b-quant
  runtime: request-queue 16ms, inference 92ms, postproc 10ms -> total 118ms
Observations: when latency spikes, request-queue is the biggest contributor (hundreds of ms). Those periods match spikes in Dedicated pool queue length.

Diagnostic commands I ran on staging/dedicated cluster:
- kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool -o wide | grep rerank
- kubectl top pod rerank-quant-xyz (cpu/mem) during spike -> CPU saturated on 3/4 pods (85-95%); memory stable.
- curl -X POST to internal /internal/validate-emb -d '{"embedding_length":1536}' -> returns 200 when correct, 400 when I intentionally send 1024.
- redis-cli MONITOR to watch cache hits: saw bursts of cache misses right before spikes.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Upstream encoder occasionally emits smaller-dimension embeddings (1024) due to model-rotation when switching to quantized lower-capacity encoder. A routing bug may pair a 1024-dim encoder with a rerank model expecting 1536.
   - Evidence: dimension in error (1024) matches size of our older embedding model. Linked PR changed default encoder flag 6 days ago.
2) A batching optimization path (dynamic concatenation) in the rerank runtime fails to validate per-example dims before stacking, leading to assert only at runtime later and larger queue times while server attempts to coerce tensors.
   - Evidence: latency spikes coincide with queue length; stack traces show numpy reshape errors inside batch assembly.
3) Network/transcoding bug where embeddings compressed via msgpack/gzip are unintentionally truncated when passing through a gateway that enforces 64KB body limits under heavy load. Truncation yields shorter vectors.
   - Evidence against: no proxy 413 logs seen; payload sizes for embeddings typically small-ish but could hit limits if candidate lists large.
4) Client SDK bug where when using 'candidate_pool: fast' the client automatically requests a compact encoder variant (1024) but still posts to same rerank endpoint — mismatch only visible when customer uses that combo.
   - Need to check SDK releases 1.8.0 -> 1.8.2 for change logs.

Quick reproduction notes:
- When I forced a 1024-dim embedding and POSTed, server responded instantly with 400. So the error path is exercised quickly and should be recoverable client-side by validating dims before sending.
- The scary case is mixed batches: if a single request has correct dims but batched alongside truncated ones, the batch assembly tries to pad/stack and causes longer latencies as it retries or waits for the batch to fill.

Proposed immediate mitigations (fast fixes):
- Add strict request-level precheck at API gateway: verify embedding lengths for query and all candidates before routing to rerank. If mismatch -> 400 with clear error, avoid queuing to dedicated pool. (low-risk ops change)
- Roll back encoder default flag in PR X that enabled compact encoder for some customers. (needs release)
- Increase request body limit logs and add counters for truncated message events on gateway (observability).

Longer-term fixes / infra items:
- Add per-batch element dimension validation in runtime before stack; reject quietly with metrics increment so we don't incur batch queue costs.
- Add unit test for mixed-dimension batches to serving-runtime test harness.
- Add analytics alert: rate of DimensionMismatchError > 5/hr triggers pager.

Notes on customers observed / impact:
- Customer A (cid_384): saw 15 failed requests across 00:30-01:00, no data leak, only 400 responses. Customer called Support.
- Customer B (cid_477): experienced timeouts (gateway 504) during spike windows because their caller retried on 400->504 incorrectly.

Debug timeline (quick):
- 2026-03-07 22:34 - first customer report via support
- 2026-03-07 22:50 - I pulled logs, saw first DimensionMismatchError entries
- 2026-03-08 00:10 - reproduced locally by truncating embeddings, validated server 400 path
- 2026-03-08 00:45 - ran pod CPU checks, observed saturation coincident with spikes
- 2026-03-08 02:00 - hotfix: added gateway precheck on staging; no spike observed in short smoke test

Commands / snippets to reproduce locally quickly:
- python3 -c 'import requests, json; q=[0.1]*1536; c=[[0.2]*1536 for _ in range(10)]; r=requests.post("https://staging.api/rerank", json={"query_embedding":q, "candidate_embeddings":c}); print(r.status_code, r.text)'
- python3 -c "import requests; q=[0.1]*1024; c=[[0.2]*1536]; r=requests.post('https://staging.api/rerank', json={'query_embedding':q,'candidate_embeddings':c}); print(r.status_code, r.text)"

Unresolved questions / TODOs for handoff:
- [ ] Confirm whether encoder rollout PR toggled default for subset of customers (check feature flags and releases).
- [ ] Add logging to gateway that includes original payload dimensions (no PII) for rapid correlation.
- [ ] Validate SDK changelog and customer versions; reach out to Support for customers using older SDKs.
- [ ] Decide whether to implement immediate precheck on production gateway (I propose yes, low blast radius).

Notes to self before I sign off:
- Keep this as a personal breadcrumb — we'll formalize into a postmortem if the metric shows recurrence.
- Slack: #eng-embeddings and #sre with summary + small runbook snippet.
- If I don't hear back by EOD, trigger page for infra on-call to deploy gateway precheck.

End of scratchpad.
